Gluttonous describes someone (or something) that consumes far more than what is needed or reasonable — driven by greed and a total lack of self-control. It is an intensely negative word. It does not just mean "eating a lot" or "wanting more." It means consuming in a way that is excessive, shameless, and greedy.

Think of it this way: if a normal person eats until they are full and stops, a gluttonous person keeps going — not because they are still hungry, but because they simply cannot (or will not) stop themselves.
The Two Ways It Is Used

1. Literally — About Food and Eating

This is the most common and traditional use. A gluttonous person eats enormous amounts of food, far beyond their body's need, and they do it selfishly and greedily.

"He was so gluttonous that he ate three full meals meant for the entire family by himself."

"Her gluttonous eating habits shocked everyone at the dinner table."

The key idea here is excess + greed + no self-restraint. It is not about being a big eater — it is about being an uncontrollably greedy eater.

2. Figuratively — About Anything Consumed Greedily

Gluttonous is also used beyond food. It can describe an obsessive, greedy craving for anything — power, money, attention, pleasure, or resources.

"The gluttonous corporation bought up every small business in town, never satisfied."

"He had a gluttonous appetite for fame — no amount of recognition was ever enough."

In this sense, you are calling someone insatiably greedy — not just about food, but about life in general.

Gluttonous is never a neutral word. It always carries strong disapproval and judgment. When you call someone gluttonous, you are saying they are:

  • Greedy — they want more than their fair share
  • Selfish — their consumption often comes at a cost to others
  • Without discipline — they have surrendered control to their desire
  • Shameless — they do not seem bothered by their excess

This is why gluttony has historically been considered a moral failing, not just a bad habit.
The Difference Between "Gluttonous" and Similar Words

• Hungry — you need food. Gluttonous — you consume far beyond need.
  • Greedy — greedy is broad (wanting more of anything). Gluttonous is more vivid and visceral — it paints a picture of unrestrained, animal-like consumption.
  • Voracious — this also means consuming a lot, but it is far less negative. You can call someone voraciously curious as a compliment. You would never call someone gluttonously curious — gluttonous is almost always an insult.
  • Indulgent — mild and sometimes positive (an indulgent dessert). Gluttonous is never mild or positive.

Knowing the related words helps cement the meaning:

  • Glutton (noun) — the person who is gluttonous. "He is a glutton."
  • Gluttony (noun) — the quality or act of being gluttonous. "Gluttony is considered one of the seven deadly sins."
  • Gluttonously (adverb) — in a gluttonous manner. "She ate gluttonously."
  • Gluttonous (adjective) — the describing word. "A gluttonous feast."
One Line to Remember It Forever

Gluttonous = excessively and greedily consuming, well beyond need, with no self-control.

If you ever see this word, picture someone who has everything they need but keeps grabbing for more anyway — not out of necessity, but out of pure, unchecked greed. That image is gluttonous.
